title: Azure Seeks 20% Cost Cut While Raising Pay for AI Talent
summary:
The Microsoft cloud business saw its annual revenue grow 40% to $101.9 billion in the year through June, but free cash flow has declined due to the massive expense of AI data centers. President Girish Bablani has since asked leaders in the 11,500 person Azure unit to identify potential savings of at least 20%, The Information reports, as quarterly free cash flow fell 20% year over year. This efficiency drive is happening as executives simultaneously increase salaries and AI budgets to compete with rivals Meta and Anthropic for engineering talent.

A spokesperson for Microsoft denied that Azure leadership has instructed teams to develop cost-reduction strategies. These reports emerge as the company reorganizes the division around Arun Ulag, executive vice president of databases, and as cloud chief Scott Guthrie advocates for expanded budget allocations for personnel to sustain the company's artificial intelligence growth.
